verses.1:1: The burden concerning Nineveh. The book of the vision of Nahum the Elkoshite.
verses.1:2: The Lord is a jealous God and takes vengeance; the Lord takes vengeance and possesses fury; the Lord takes vengeance against His foes, and He Himself is angry with His enemies.
verses.1:3: The Lord is patient and great in strength, and cleansing, He will not make one innocent. The Lord has His ways in the storm and the whirlwind, and the clouds are the dust of His feet.
verses.1:4: He rebukes the sea and dries it up, and brings all the rivers to a desert. Bashan and Carmel have grown weak, and the flower of Lebanon has wilted.
verses.1:5: The mountains have been shaken by Him, and the hills have been made desolate; and the earth has trembled before His face, and the world, and all who dwell in it.
verses.1:6: Before the face of His indignation, who will stand? And who will resist in the wrath of His fury? His indignation has been poured out like fire, and the rocks have been dissolved by Him.
verses.1:7: The Lord is good, and gives strength in the day of distress, and knows those who hope in Him.
verses.1:8: And with a flood passing through, He will make a full end of its place, and darkness will pursue His enemies.
verses.1:9: What are you devising against the Lord? He Himself will make a full end; a double distress will not rise up,
verses.1:10: for just as thorns entwine one another, so is their banquet as they drink together; they will be consumed like stubble full of dryness.
verses.1:11: From you will go forth one devising wickedness against the Lord, pondering transgression in his mind.
verses.1:12: This is what the Lord says: "If they are complete and so many, even so they will be shorn, and he will pass away; I have afflicted you, and I will not afflict you any longer.
verses.1:13: And now I will shatter his rod from your back, and I will burst your bonds."
verses.1:14: And the Lord will give a command concerning you: "No more will be sown from your name; from the house of your god I will destroy the carved image and the cast image; I will make your grave, because you are dishonored."
verses.1:15: Look, on the mountains are the feet of one proclaiming good news and announcing peace. Celebrate your festivals, Judah, and pay your vows, for Belial will no longer pass through you; he has wholly perished.
verses.2:1: One has come up who will scatter before you, who will maintain the siege: watch the road, strengthen your loins, fortify your might greatly.
verses.2:2: For the Lord has restored the pride of Jacob, like the pride of Israel; because devastators have laid them waste, and have ruined their shoots.
verses.2:3: The shield of his mighty men is fiery, the men of the army are in scarlet; the reins of the chariot are fiery on the day of his preparation, and the drivers have been lulled into a stupor.
verses.2:4: On the roads they have been thrown into confusion; the chariots have collided in the squares; their appearance is like torches, like flashes of lightning darting about.
verses.2:5: He will remember his mighty men; they will fall on their roads; swiftly they will climb her walls, and the shelter will be prepared.
verses.2:6: The gates of the rivers have been opened, and the temple has been demolished to the ground.
verses.2:7: And the soldier has been led away captive, and her maidservants were being driven along, moaning like doves, murmuring in their hearts.
verses.2:8: And Nineveh, her waters are like a pool of waters; yet they themselves have fled. "Stand, stand!" and there is no one who turns back.
verses.2:9: Plunder the silver, plunder the gold: and there is no end to the riches from all the desirable vessels.
verses.2:10: She is laid waste, and split, and torn apart; and a melting heart, and a loosening of the knees, and a failing in all loins, and the faces of all of them are like the blackness of a pot.
verses.2:11: Where is the dwelling place of the lions, and the feeding ground of the lion cubs, to which the lion went so that the lion cub might enter there, and there is no one to terrify them?
verses.2:12: The lion seized enough for his cubs, and killed for his lionesses, and filled his caves with prey, and his lair with plunder.
verses.2:13: "Look, I am against you," says the Lord of hosts, "and I will burn your chariots up into smoke, and the sword will consume your young lions, and I will wipe out your prey from the earth, and the voice of your messengers will no longer be heard."
verses.3:1: Woe, city of bloodshed, wholly full of the tearing apart of falsehood! Plunder will not depart from you.
verses.3:2: The sound of the whip, and the sound of the rushing of the wheel, and of the snorting horse, and of the surging chariot, and of the mounting horseman,
verses.3:3: and of the flashing sword, and of the glittering spear, and of a slaughtered multitude, and of heavy ruin; and there is no end to the corpses, and they will collapse over their bodies.
verses.3:4: Because of the multitude of the fornications of the prostitute, beautiful and charming and possessing sorceries, who sold nations through her fornications and families through her sorceries.
verses.3:5: "Look, I am against you," says the Lord of hosts, "and I will uncover your shameful parts to your face; and I will show the nations your nakedness, and the kingdoms your disgrace.
verses.3:6: And I will throw abominations upon you, and I will subject you to insults, and I will make you an example.
verses.3:7: And it will be: everyone who sees you will recoil from you and will say, 'Nineveh has been devastated.' Who will shake his head over you? From where will I seek a comforter for you?"
verses.3:8: Are you any better than Alexandria of the peoples, who dwells among the rivers? Waters are all around her, whose wealth is the sea; waters are her walls.
verses.3:9: Ethiopia was her strength, and Egypt, and there is no end; Africa and the Libyans were for your help.
verses.3:10: Yet even she herself was led into exile, into captivity: her little ones were dashed to pieces at the head of all the streets, and over her honored men they cast lots, and all her leading men were fastened in shackles.
verses.3:11: And so you also will become drunk, and you will be despised; and you will seek help from the enemy.
verses.3:12: All your fortresses are like fig trees with their unripe figs: if they are shaken, they will fall into the mouth of the eater.
verses.3:13: Look, your people are women in your midst: to your enemies the gates of your land will be thrown wide open; fire will devour your bars.
verses.3:14: Draw water for yourself for the siege: build up your fortresses, go into the clay and tread it; kneading it, take hold of the brick.
verses.3:15: There fire will consume you, you will perish by the sword, it will devour you like the young locust: gather together like the young locust, multiply like the locust.
verses.3:16: You have made your trading ventures more numerous than the stars of the sky; the young locust has spread out and flown away.
verses.3:17: Your guards are like locusts, and your little ones are like locusts of locusts, which settle in the hedges on a day of cold: the sun has risen, and they have flown away, and their place where they were is not known.
verses.3:18: Your shepherds have slumbered, king of Assyria, your princes will be buried; your people have hidden in the mountains, and there is no one to gather them.
verses.3:19: Your shattering is not hidden; your wound is most severe. All who have heard the report about you have clapped their hands together over you; for over whom has your wickedness not always passed?

notes.1:3: The Vulgate renders the Hebrew emphatic construction literally as 'cleansing, He will not make one innocent' (mundans non faciet innocentem), meaning He will by no means acquit the guilty. The Latin also reads plural 'His ways' (viae ejus) where the Hebrew has singular 'His way'.
notes.1:7: Where the Hebrew reads 'a stronghold' and 'those who take refuge in Him', the Vulgate renders 'gives strength' (confortans) and 'those who hope in Him' (sperantes in se).
notes.1:12: Latin pertransibit ('he will pass away') shifts abruptly to the singular after plural attondentur ('they will be shorn'), mirroring the Hebrew syntax.
notes.1:13: The Vulgate distinctly reads 'his rod from your back' (virgam ejus de dorso tuo), whereas the Hebrew has 'his yoke from upon you'.
notes.1:15: In native Clementine Vulgate numbering (Clem1598-USFX), this verse concludes chapter 1 as 1:15 (mapped to Saints.Bible 2:1, shifting 2:1-13 one verse relative to Saints 2:2-14). The Vulgate retains Belial as a proper name rather than translating it as 'the wicked one'.
notes.2:1: The Vulgate renders qui custodiat obsidionem ('who will maintain the siege') as a second relative clause describing the attacker, whereas the Hebrew shifts to an imperative addressed to Nineveh ('guard the rampart').
notes.2:3: The Vulgate has two notable readings here: 'the reins of the chariot are fiery' (igneae habenae currus; Hebrew 'the chariots flash with steel') and 'the drivers have been lulled into a stupor' (agitatores consopiti sunt; Hebrew 'the cypress spears are brandished').
notes.2:7: The Vulgate distinctly reads 'the soldier' (miles) for the difficult Hebrew hutzav, and 'murmuring in their hearts' (murmurantes in cordibus suis) where the Hebrew has 'beating their breasts'. Late Latin minabantur (passive of mino) means 'were being driven along'.
notes.2:8: The Vulgate reads 'her waters' (aquae ejus) where the Hebrew has 'from her days' ('of old').
notes.3:5: Where the Hebrew says 'I will lift up your skirts over your face', the Vulgate translates explicitly as 'I will uncover your shameful parts to your face' (revelabo pudenda tua in facie tua).
notes.3:8: The Vulgate distinctly identifies the city as 'Alexandria of the peoples' (Alexandria populorum), rendering the Hebrew No-Amon (Thebes in Egypt).
notes.3:9: The Vulgate renders the Hebrew Put as Africa. Like the Hebrew text, the Latin shifts in the second clause from third person ('her strength') to second person ('for your help', in auxilio tuo).
notes.3:17: Where the Hebrew refers to military officials ('your marshals' or 'your scribes'), the Vulgate distinctly reads 'your little ones' (parvuli tui) and renders the Hebrew swarm idiom literally as 'locusts of locusts' (locustae locustarum).
notes.3:18: The Vulgate distinctly reads 'your princes will be buried' (sepelientur principes tui) and 'your people have hidden' (latitavit populus tuus), where the Hebrew has 'your nobles sleep' and 'your people are scattered'.
